channel.title: Molecular & Cell Biology Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Cell Biology, Molecular Cell, Nature Structural & Molecular Biology, and The EMBO Journal.

item.title: Molecular Cell: An epigenetic program dictates MYC amplification dynamics that promote transient, extrachromosomal, and inherited genomic events
item.description: Ferman et al. demonstrate that epigenetic imbalance directly controls MYC oncogene amplification dynamics, which identifies possible biomarkers and therapeutic targets for aggressive tumors. When a cell-death checkpoint fails, the low MYC copy gains expand to high levels, which include circular and integrated events and associate with tumorigenesis.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: A dual-action bacteriophage protein Ped1 degrades DNA and blocks replication in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
The EMBO Journal: A conserved archaeal protein with evolutionary links to bacterial ribosome hibernation and eukaryotic energy sensing
The EMBO Journal: Leptin-sensitive hypothalamic Lepr+/Glp1r + neurons limit hyperphagia and weight gain in diet-induced obesity
Nature Cell Biology: Quantification of lipid sorting during clathrin-mediated endocytosis
item.description: Lennartz et al. evaluate lipid enrichment in clathrin-coated pits and observe that the differential lipid partitioning into clathrin-coated pits is largely driven by the lipid asymmetry of the plasma membrane.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Transcription factor clusters enhance gene expression in vivo without modulating bursting dynamics
item.description: Cadar et al. show that the transcription factor Dorsal forms clusters at genes carrying many binding sites in living fly embryos. Losing these clusters is lethal, yet they do not switch genes on; they merely boost output from already-active genes, challenging prevailing views of how condensates control transcription.

item.title: Molecular Cell: The early RNA decay factor ZC3H18 directs first intron splicing
item.description: Le Rest et al. identify ZC3H18 as the long-sought molecular link between the cap-binding complex (CBC) and first intron splicing. ZC3H18 recruits early splicing factors through interactions that are mutually exclusive with RNA decay factor binding, implying how cap-bound nascent transcripts are directed toward productive splicing rather than degradation.

item.title: Molecular Cell: ATM safeguards DNA replication by restraining pathological repriming at endogenous base lesions
item.description: Sommerova et al. show that ataxia telangiectasia-mutated (ATM) protects replicating cells by restraining pathological bypass of endogenous oxidative base lesions through PRIMPOL-mediated repriming. When ATM is lost, post-replicative adducted ssDNA gaps accumulate, creating dependence on homologous recombination for repair and driving PARP hyperactivation and PARP inhibitor sensitivity.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Cotranslational membrane protein biogenesis by an EMC-bound translocon
item.description: The authors use selective ribosome profiling, cryo-ET and site-specific photocrosslinking to show how the ER membrane protein complex (EMC) cooperates with ribosome-bound translocons to facilitate multipass membrane protein biogenesis in human cells.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Profiling extracellular vesicle glycoRNAs defines their function in vesicular communication
item.description: The authors expand the extracellular vesicle glycosylated RNA (glycoRNA) landscape and reveal distinct glycoRNA profiles across extracellular vesicle (EV) subtypes, cell types and passage numbers. They also show that glycoRNAs are not only EV cargoes but also regulators of EV uptake, uncovering a layer of vesicle-mediated communication.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: HERC4-mediated ubiquitination licenses RIPK1 to initiate TNF-induced cell death
item.description: Lu and Du et al. show that HERC4 E3 ligase ubiquitinates S166-phosphorylated RIPK1 to initiate prodeath complex assembly and TNF-induced cell death, acting as the pivotal prodeath switch and that loss of HERC4 protects mice from TNF-driven inflammation and liver injury.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: A functional screen for bacterial ubiquitin regulation identifies an unusual Pseudomonas aeruginosa E3 ligase
The EMBO Journal: MCM10 and SLD-2/RECQL4 jointly activate the CMG helicase during metazoan DNA replication initiation
The EMBO Journal: Excess Met1-linked ubiquitination leads to solid aggregate formation
The EMBO Journal: Clustering of host N-glycans by the microneme MIC1/4/6 complex licenses Toxoplasma rhoptry discharge
Nature Cell Biology: Taxane-induced conformational changes in the microtubule lattice activate GEF-H1-dependent RhoA signalling
item.description: Meiring, Mahapatra et al. show that expanded microtubule lattice conformations, such as those induced by small-molecule taxanes, can lead to the release of GEF-H1 and thus induce RhoA activation.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Simplifying in silico protein evolution with minimal screening by unZipro
item.description: Qin et al. present unZipro, a geometric deep learning framework that adapts general protein design models to specific protein families. By leveraging meta-learning, unZipro efficiently navigates family-specific fitness landscapes, enabling rapid protein evolution across gene editing, luciferase reporting, transcriptional regulation, and antiviral resistance with minimal experimental screening.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Whole genome duplication through mitotic slippage causes nuclear instability
The EMBO Journal: The BRCA1 coiled-coil domain is dispensable for suppression of tandem duplications and tolerance of FANCM loss
The EMBO Journal: Transgenerational inheritance of altered H3K27me3 in wild-type Caenorhabditis elegans
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Mechanistic insights into phosphorylation-driven activation and therapeutic inhibition of human ATR–ATRIP
item.description: Wang et al. present cryo-electron microscopy structures of ATR–ATRIP complexes in distinct functional states, revealing ATP-dependent and TopBP1-dependent mechanisms of kinase activation and how ATR inhibitors exploit ATP-binding pocket flexibility for selective inhibition.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: ZEP1 orchestrates template choice and crossover pathways to ensure meiotic genome integrity in rice
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structure-guided discovery and engineering of miniature CRISPR–Cas12m for epigenome editing
item.description: The authors identified and engineered a miniature, innate nuclease-dead xCas12m enabling effective epigenome editing. xCas12m–CRISPRoff achieved durable epigenetic silencing and inhibition of hepatitis B virus infection through single-AAV delivery.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: The Batten disease protein CLN8 is a stereospecific acyltransferase in bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate biosynthesis
item.description: Two studies show that the endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein CLN8 catalyses the acyl CoA-dependent acylation of glycerophosphoglycerol, producing lysophosphatidylglycerol, which is then converted into bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate. These results provide insight into CLN8 Batten disease.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Batten disease protein CLN8 enables a non-canonical phospholipid synthesis pathway
item.description: Two studies show that the ER-associated protein CLN8 catalyses the acyl CoA-dependent acylation of glycerophosphoglycerol, producing lysophosphatidylglycerol, which is then converted into BMP. These results provide insight into CLN8 Batten disease.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: DFCP1-containing ER microdomains mediate lysosomal membrane repair
item.description: Radulovic et al. show that phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P), produced by the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase PIK3C3, is formed on ER domains after lysosome damage. ER domain PI3P helps to recruit the ATPase DFCP1, which promotes lysosome repair.

item.title: Molecular Cell: 5-Azacytosine induces cytotoxicity via 5-methylcytosine depletion on chromatin-associated RNA in leukemia
item.description: Gao et al. reveal that the clinically used drug 5-azacytidine (5-azaC) induces transcriptional repression through RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C) depletion, rather than acting solely as a DNA hypomethylating agent. Loss of m5C disrupts both MBD6-mediated H2AK119ub removal and SRSF2-mediated H3K27ac deposition, triggering leukemia cell death via cell-cycle disruption and defective DNA repair.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Hox / Meis -dependent gene-regulatory transition underlies cardiopharyngeal neural crest diversification
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Cryo-EM structure, enzymatic activity and genome targeting of canonical PRC1
item.description: Ciapponi et al. determine the cryo-electron microscopy structure of the canonical Polycomb repressive complex 1 holocomplex and show how its architecture coordinates complex assembly, H2A monoubiquitination and genomic targeting.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Microtubule posttranslational modifications provide unique recognition patterns for associated proteins
Nature Cell Biology: 4D nucleome landscape reveals dissolution of bipartite active X chromosome in liver cancer development
item.description: Xie, Tan, Mo and colleagues show that a liver-specific bipartite structure of the active X chromosome is lost early in hepatocarcinogenesis in mice and humans, driving X-linked gene activation and premalignant transformation, particularly in males.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Gain-of-function suppressors restore microtubule dynamics and rescue dominant-negative tubulinopathies
item.description: Xu, Guo et al. report suppressor screens in Caenorhabditis elegans to counteract tubulin mutants. They report several missense variants in tubulin genes that may restore microtubule architecture and dynamics, which may have some conservation in mammalian cells.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: ATP-independent unfolding of ubiquitin by Ufd1 initiates Cdc48/p97-mediated substrate processing
item.description: Wang et al. show that the UT3 domain of Ufd1 binds to and unfolds K48-linked polyubiquitin chains without ATP. Simultaneous binding of two ubiquitins to UT3 is key to overcome the energy barrier. This ubiquitin unfolding is critical for Cdc48/p97’s function.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: The periphery of nuclear speckles defines a spatially and temporally regulated compartment of long-lived intron-retained RNAs that resolves during mitosis
item.description: Biayna, Baranovskii and colleagues report that intron-retained RNAs derived from cell cycle- and genome maintenance-related genes are pooled at the periphery of nuclear speckles and undergo synchronous splicing at mitosis, thereby contributing to their temporal regulation.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Pre-activation and gating pathway of AMPA receptors revealed by full and partial agonists
item.description: AMPA receptor (AMPAR) gating proceeds through an intermediate pre-active state that has structurally remained an enigma. Here, Newton et al. use full and partial agonists and time-resolved cryo-electron microscopy to resolve this state and reveal the complete gating pathway of AMPARs.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural mechanisms for ATP-mediated inhibition of human NLRP6 inflammasome
item.description: Cui, Sheng and colleagues present cryo-EM structures of human NLRP6 monomer in the ATP/NBD-bound and ATP/NBD-unbound conformations, revealing the detailed mechanisms of how ATP acts as an endogenous inhibitor of the NLRP6 inflammasome.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Tissue flow acts as a guidance cue for immune cell polarization and directional migration
item.description: Le et al. show that in Xenopus embryos, local ectodermal tissue flows provide a directional cue that polarizes and guides embryonic myeloid cells migration via cell-on-cell interactions.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: KDM6A loss enhances oxidative phosphorylation uncovering tissue-level convergent evolution
Nature Cell Biology: Multi-stromal organoid co-culture modelling reveals epithelial–fibroblast heterogeneity in pancreatic cancer and pancreatitis
item.description: Li, Jihad and colleagues develop an organoid co-culture system, alongside patient tissue and mouse model analyses, to model, characterize and compare cellular interactions between epithelia and stroma in pancreatitis versus pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Molecular architecture and spatial organization of proteasomes in the human sperm nucleus
item.description: Proteasomes are essential for male fertility. Kolata, dos Santos, Dendooven and colleagues show large nuclear proteasomal assemblies segregated from DNA in human sperm, forming after meiosis and with a unique α4s isoform. A native substrate is bound at the 20S catalytic site.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Presynaptic accumulation of APP-CTFβ may contribute to synaptic dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: A single-amino-acid cleavage controls global mitochondrial complex integrity
item.description: Kücükköse, Luzarowski and colleagues show that removing a single N-terminal amino acid during the maturation of newly imported mitochondrial proteins globally stabilizes mitochondrial protein complexes, revealing an unexpected layer of regulation of mitochondrial proteostasis.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Repositioning of polyubiquitin alters the pathologic tau filament structure
item.description: Watanabe et al. show that tau fibrils from Alzheimer disease and vacuolar tauopathy exhibit distinct seeding patterns in vivo. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals that modifications outside the ordered core can remodel tau fibril ultrastructure, with polyubiquitin repositioning of vacuolar tauopathy fibrils shifting the protofilament interface.

item.title: Molecular Cell: dsRNAscan maps human dsRNAome, revealing conservation, intermolecular dsRNA, and correlates of ADAR dependency
item.description: Andrews and Bass develop dsRNAscan to predict millions of double-stranded RNA structures across the human genome. ADAR editing and structure-probing data classify ∼2.4 million predictions as high-confidence, enabling prediction of intermolecular dsRNAs, conserved dsRNAs, and quantification of dsRNA burden as a correlate of cell death after ADAR knockout.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Structural and mechanistic insights into gating and allosteric modulation of GluN1–GluN3A NMDA receptors
item.description: Kim et al. present cryo-EM structures of GluN1–GluN3A NMDA receptors with complementary electrophysiology, revealing structure-based mechanisms of receptor gating, paradoxical potentiation by a GluN1-selective antagonist and allosteric modulation.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Response of the replisome to araA and araC suggests a mechanism for arabinosyl nucleoside tolerance
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Characterizing dynamics of productive dynein stepping by MINFLUX
item.description: Slivka et al. track dynein’s microtubule-binding domain with minimal fluorescence photon flux, revealing transient backward ‘dips’ before steps. These dips represent microtubule release upon ATP binding and diffusional search, terminating in net forward bias driven by ATP hydrolysis.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: The proportional scaling of mRNA and ribosome concentrations controls eukaryotic cell growth
item.description: Gao et al. show that yeast grow faster by proportionally increasing mRNA and ribosome concentrations to increase actively translating ribosomes, while elongation remains constant. A mass-action model explains growth-rate changes.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Elevated contractility drives implantation failure in mouse embryos from aged females
item.description: Cavanaugh et al. show that embryos from aged mice have increased contractility and tissue viscosity on embryonic day 4.5, which leads to poor spreading and attachment. Similar age-associated mechanical changes in human embryos correlate with implantation potential.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: CD137 agonists in mice suppress germinal center responses by increasing the immunosuppressive activity of follicular regulatory T-cells
Nature Cell Biology: Circadian control of circulating tumour-derived extracellular vesicle secretion affects targeted therapy efficacy
item.description: Chen, Zhang and colleagues report ctEV-CLOCK as a tool to characterize circulating tumour-derived extracellular vesicles and demonstrate a pattern of circadian oscillation, which may be leveraged to design time-synchronized targeted cancer therapy.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Loss of Erbin in tubular epithelial cells sensitizes mice to acute kidney injury and aggravates renal fibrosis
The EMBO Journal: Anchoring of perforin-2 via the transmembrane domain is required for antigen escape into the cytosol
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Hydrophobic interactions of FG-nucleoporins are required for dilating nuclear membrane pores into selective transport channels after mitosis
item.description: Zhang et al. show that FG-nucleoporins self-assemble through hydrophobic interactions to dilate newly assembling nuclear pores after mitosis, enabling nuclear import and nuclear expansion, which in turn remodel the nuclear envelope.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Disease-specific tau polymorphs are associated with unique protein networks across proteinopathies
The EMBO Journal: Nested TAD hierarchy defines cohesion zones on replicated chromosomes
The EMBO Journal: Canonical and non-canonical miRNA degradation shapes state transitions and stemness in breast cancer
The EMBO Journal: Reconstitution of glycan-driven MHC-I recycling reveals calreticulin as mediator between TAPBPR and tapasin
The EMBO Journal: FAF1 and FAF2 enhance unfolding by p97-UFD1-NPL4 complex enabling rational design of p97 activators
Nature Cell Biology: An EZH2–SREBP2 axis promotes cholesterol biosynthesis and represents a noncanonical vulnerability in tumorigenesis
item.description: Kim et al. demonstrate a non-canonical function for EZH2 in modulating cholesterol metabolism and tumour development by interacting with SREBP2, which may be targeted by PROTACs to disrupt its oncogenic activity.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Engineering editopes through programmable RNA editing toward tumor neoantigen generation
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Nucleosomes and IDRs suppress promiscuous GCN4 binding on minichromosomes
item.description: Wei et al. measure single-molecule kinetics of transcription factor GCN4 on purified yeast minichromosomes to reveal that both nucleosomes and transcription factor intrinsically disordered regions facilitate GCN4 target search on native chromatin by shortening its promiscuous binding.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: The calcium-binding protein CSE links Ca 2+ signaling with cell-cell communication in cyanobacteria
The EMBO Journal: Orally available Colivin traps TRPV3 in an inactive state and suppresses intestinal inflammation
The EMBO Journal: Principles of ribosome-associated protein quality control during the synthesis of CFTR
The EMBO Journal: Chromatin condensates tune nuclear mechanosensing and preserve nuclear integrity to prevent cGAS activation
Nature Cell Biology: Mega-enhancers compartmentalize transcriptionally active long genes in the brain
item.description: Zhao et al. describe an enhancer-dense nuclear microenvironment in the cerebellum that includes long neuronal genes and mega-enhancers. This microenvironment partly depends on the transcription factor Etv1 and is dynamic during neuronal maturation.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: In-situ cryo-ET of mouse embryos reveals cytoplasmic lattices contain ubiquitin-charged E2-E3 ligase assemblies
Nature Cell Biology: Targeting oncogenic FLT3 uncovers a ferroptosis vulnerability through selenocysteine recoding in acute myeloid leukaemia
item.description: Li et al. report that FLT3 inhibition impairs selenoprotein translation and induces ferroptosis to suppress FLT3 -mutant leukaemia. This can be counteracted by dietary vitamin E, which may disrupt the efficacy of tyrosine kinase inhibitors in treatment of acute myeloid leukaemia.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: The mitochondria enzyme OGDH defends against disulfidptosis by licensing METTL3-regulated NRF2 translation
item.description: Chen, Xu, Zhou, Wu et al. report that a citric acid cycle enzyme OGDH regulates METTL3 succinylation and its activation as an m6A reader, thereby modulating NRF2 translation, disulfidptosis evasion and tumour growth.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Pho84/GLUT2 are cellular myo -inositol exporters regulated by inositol pyrophosphates
The EMBO Journal: Allosteric switching of Ca 2+ permeability in the lysosomal ion channel TPC2 underpins biased agonist activation
Nature Cell Biology: CLOCK/BMAL1 interactome uncovers homeodomain factors as tissue regulators
item.description: Aygenli et al. map chromatin-bound CLOCK/BMAL1 protein complexes across three mouse tissues and uncover PROX1, HNF1B and HOXA5 as homeodomain cofactors that directly bind and co-occupy BMAL1 sites to establish tissue-specific circadian transcription.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Stromal cell senescence augments haematopoietic cell fitness in clonal haematopoiesis
item.description: Mistry et al. propose that Dnmt3a -mutant haematopoietic cells induce mesenchymal stromal cell senescence. Removal of senescent non-haematopoietic cells reduces Dnmt3a -mutant haematopoiesis.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Distinct amyloid-β filament fold in individuals with APP Flemish mutation
item.description: Brain samples from individuals with the rare APP Flemish mutation reveal a distinct amyloid-β filament fold that may help explain the accumulation of amyloid-β in blood vessels in inherited Alzheimer disease.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: BRD4 recruitment into HP1 condensates desilences transcription without erasure of repressive chromatin
item.description: Brandon, Robinson-Thiewes, Kaulage et al. report that targeted BRD4 recruitment enables transcription through H3K9me3/HP1-marked heterochromatin without erasing repressive marks, identifying condensate partitioning as a mechanism for gene desilencing.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Damage recognition by intestinal stem cells via Draper promotes adult Drosophila midgut regeneration
The EMBO Journal: P-selectin delineates conserved functional heterogeneity in early hematopoietic stem cell aging in humans and mice
The EMBO Journal: Membrane lipid composition and rapid endocytic retrieval modulate Wingless secretion
Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Variant characterization in the intrinsically disordered human proteome
item.description: Proteome-wide prediction and structural modeling of disordered protein interaction interfaces advance characterization of disease-associated variants in disordered protein regions.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Factors modulating the assembly of human β 2 -adrenergic receptor–β-arrestin complexes
item.description: Wilhelm, Pluhackova and colleagues show how ligand binding, receptor phosphorylation and membrane interactions, including PIP 2 , drive the assembly of human β 2 -adrenergic receptor–β-arrestin complexes, providing insight into structural mechanisms regulating GPCR signaling.

item.title: Nature Structural & Molecular Biology: Protein thiol alterations drive pathologic liquid–liquid phase separation in the aging brain
item.description: Vignane et al. show that age-related protein oxidation disrupts normal brain protein organization, promoting harmful condensates and aggregation linked to neurodegeneration, whereas hydrogen sulfide-driven persulfidation counteracts these effects.

item.title: The EMBO Journal: Polo/PLK1 phosphorylation relieves Centrosomin/Cnn autoinhibition to promote centrosome scaffold assembly
The EMBO Journal: NF-κB/RelA signaling required for CD40-induced humoral immunity depends on specific NEMO lysine residues in mice
The EMBO Journal: The Arabidopsis SPFH protein HIR2 modulates receptor signaling and plasma membrane organization
The EMBO Journal: RAD54L coordinates the nucleolar DNA damage response to maintain rDNA stability
The EMBO Journal: FUS controls muscle differentiation through phase separation-mediated recruitment of the transcription factors MEF2 and ETV5
The EMBO Journal: Tripartite ER-mitochondria-lipid droplets contact sites control adipocyte metabolic flexibility
